correctness.rationale: For complements, all nonzero Fourier samples have the same modulus while the zero sample changes from m to 7-m, reducing the global search to support sizes 1, 2, and 3. The one- and two-frequency cases are evaluated exactly. The 35 three-subsets split exactly into a 21-member arithmetic-progression orbit and a 14-member difference-set orbit. Their concentration ratios are derived analytically; exact minimal polynomials and rational isolating intervals show the consecutive triple strictly dominates every competing class. Equality conditions survive every reduction and give exactly seven maximizers. The packaged checker exhausts all 127 nonzero subsets only as a replay check.

value.rationale: Bonami--Révész make the unrestricted finite-cyclic p=1 concentration constant a natural object and leave best constants undetermined in their general theory. Modulus 7 is the first prime for which three-point supports split into two affine geometries; the theorem completely resolves all 127 nonzero idempotents, proves that a three-frequency consecutive block beats every one-, two-, four-, five-, six-, and seven-frequency competitor, and identifies every maximizer. This is a natural exact finite benchmark for the endpoint concentration problem rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
